items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I had never done much singing except for a few group vocals with Lloyds Scott

ctx.x: Django had an approach to the guitar unlike any other guitarist playing in the States. He had a phenomenal execution, and he was taking a lot of solos at a time when solos were not known about on the guitar as a rule. Teddy Bunn, for instance, didn't have Django's speed or technical mastery. In fact the quintet as a whole, liked to play numbers fast. However, Djano was also an excellent accompanist. He seemed to have ideas which would stray a little from the original harmonies, so there was always something which…

About two weeks after we had been in the Villa d'Este, I was asked if I would accept a job to sing in a club called "l'Heure Bleue" on rue Fromentin, after I had finished my night at the Villa d'Este. I had never done much singing except for a few group vocals with Lloyds Scott, but I knew the words to many songs and my voice was not the worst that could be hears so I thought it would be kicks to do a little singing and I accepted the proposition.

The musicians playing at l'Heure Bleue were known at the Quintet of the Hot Club de France. I had not met any of them before and had not heard them in action either until the first night I went to sing with them. I had to sing 4 numbers and then I was finished. That wasn't what anyone could call a hard job. I don't remember how much I was paid but I do remember that these musicians knew every song I wanted to sing.
